channel.title: Acura recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Honda, Acura Rear Subframe May Corrode And Fail
item.description: On these vehicles, the rear subframe can corrode at the points where the suspension is mounted. If this happens, rear suspension parts, such as the rear control arm, can fail. This affects vehicles sold in a number of states. Dealers will inspect the rear subframe and install a reinforcement kit, and repair or replace subframe components as needed, free of charge. A final remedy is expected later, and additional letters will follow once it's ready.

item.title: Honda and Acura front passenger airbags may deploy unintentionally
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Honda and Acura vehicles, including the Accord, Civic, CR-V, Odyssey, Pilot, Ridgeline, HR-V, Fit, Insight, Passport and the Acura TLX, RDX and MDX. The sensor that measures the weight of the person in the front passenger seat can crack and short circuit. If that happens, the airbags can go off when they should not during a crash. Dealers will replace the seat weight sensors at no cost. This recall expands an earlier recall.

item.title: Acura ZDX Rearview Camera Display Failure
item.description: On some 2024 Acura ZDX and 2024-2025 Honda Prologue vehicles, the rearview camera screen may show a distorted or blank picture instead of a clear view of what's behind the vehicle.

item.title: Acura ZDX Instrument Panel and Camera Software Failure
item.description: A software problem in some Acura ZDX vehicles can cause the instrument panel display to stop working, so drivers may not see the speedometer or warning lights. A separate software issue can make the rearview camera show a blank screen instead of the view behind the vehicle when it's in reverse. Both issues can leave drivers without information they need to drive or back up safely.

item.title: Honda and Acura Driver Seats May Be Loose
item.description: Some Honda Accord, Accord Hybrid, HR-V, Pilot, and Acura Integra vehicles may have a driver's seat cushion frame that was not tightened properly. This can leave the seat loose. A loose driver's seat may not properly hold the driver in place during a crash, which increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Acura ILX Brake Fluid Contamination Weakens Braking
item.description: In these Acura ILX vehicles, the brake fluid can become contaminated. Over time, that contamination can cause a seal inside the brake master cylinder to deform, or change shape. Once the seal deforms, brake fluid can leak out from inside the system. When fluid leaks this way, it can reduce how well the brakes work, meaning the brakes may not perform as they should when needed.

item.title: Acura RDX Power Steering Software May Fail
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Acura RDX vehicles because the software that controls the electric power steering assist may not be calibrated properly. If this happens, the steering system can enter a failsafe mode, resulting in a loss of power steering assist while driving. Dealers will reprogram the electric power steering software so it is calibrated correctly, and this repair will be done free of charge.

item.title: Acura, Honda Brake Pedal Pin Can Shift
item.description: The brake pedal in these vehicles is held in place by a pin that was not secured correctly. Because of this, the pedal can shift out of its normal position while the vehicle is being driven. When the pedal moves out of place, the driver may not be able to press the brakes the way they normally would, which can affect the vehicle's ability to slow down or stop.

item.title: Acura MDX Tailgate Lights May Fail From Moisture
item.description: In certain Acura MDX vehicles, moisture can get into the tailgate light assembly and its wiring. This can cause the interior and exterior lights to stop working, including the tailgate lid lights, position lights, license plate lights, and taillights.

item.title: Acura ZDX Stabilizer Bar Bolts May Loosen
item.description: Some Acura ZDX vehicles have passenger-side front stabilizer bar bracket bolts that may not have been tightened properly. If these bolts loosen, they can separate from the vehicle frame, and the stabilizer bar or bracket can detach. A detached part can damage the vehicle's high voltage cables or the battery coolant lines. Damage to those cables or lines can cause the vehicle to shut down and lose drive power while being driven, which increases the chance of a crash.

item.title: Acura MDX Touchscreen May Go Blank, Hiding Camera
item.description: Some 2025 Acura MDX vehicles have a touchscreen in the center console that may go blank. When this happens, the rearview camera image does not display as it should. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety rules that require a working rear visibility display. Without the camera image, the driver may not be able to see what is behind the vehicle when backing up.

item.title: Acura MDX, TLX, Honda Pilot Engine May Stall
item.description: Certain Acura MDX Type-S, Acura TLX Type-S, and Honda Pilot vehicles have a software error in the fuel injection electronic control unit, sometimes called the FI-ECU. Because of this software error, the engine may stall or lose power while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Acura ZDX Bolts May Damage High-Voltage Cables
item.description: On certain 2024 Acura ZDX vehicles, the bolts that hold the front passenger stabilizer bar bracket in place may become loose over time. If the bolts become loose enough, the bracket can detach from the vehicle's frame entirely. When this happens, the detached bracket or its bolts can damage the vehicle's high voltage cables or the coolant lines that serve the EV battery.

item.title: Acura TLX fuel tank weld may leak fuel
item.description: Certain Acura TLX cars have a fuel filler neck and fuel tank that may not have been welded together properly during manufacturing. This improper welding can allow fuel to leak out of the tank. A fuel leak is a serious problem on its own, and it becomes especially dangerous if it happens near a possible source of ignition.

item.title: Honda and Acura Models Loose Driver's Seat Frame
item.description: In these vehicles, the frame underneath the driver's seat cushion may not have been tightened properly when the vehicle was built at the factory. Because the frame isn't properly tightened, the driver's seat can end up unsecured instead of being firmly fastened in place the way it should be. This means the seating system in these vehicles does not meet the federal safety standard that covers how seats must be secured.

item.title: Honda and Acura Steering Gearbox Can Cause Difficulty Steering
item.description: Honda says the steering gearbox in these vehicles may not have been manufactured correctly. This defect can create too much internal friction inside the gearbox assembly. That extra friction can make the steering feel harder to turn, so drivers may have more difficulty steering the vehicle than they should. Honda is recalling the vehicles to fix this steering gearbox problem so the issue is corrected properly.

item.title: Acura ZDX Anti-Lock Brakes May Release Pressure
item.description: In certain all-wheel-drive ZDX vehicles, the anti-lock brake system may activate on its own and release pressure in the vehicle's regular brake system. This can happen unexpectedly while the vehicle is being driven, reducing the vehicle's ability to brake normally.

item.title: Acura RDX and Odyssey Steering Corrosion Risk
item.description: On some Acura RDX and Honda Odyssey vehicles, the steering gear box may not have been tightened properly. This can let water get inside, causing corrosion and the gears to bind. Corroded, binding gears can make the steering harder to control.

item.title: Honda and Acura passenger seat sensor may crack
item.description: Honda is recalling certain 2020 through 2022 Honda and Acura vehicles, including Accord, Civic, CR-V, HR-V, Odyssey, Pilot, Passport, Ridgeline, Fit, Insight and the Acura MDX, RDX and TLX. The sensor that measures the weight of the person in the front passenger seat can crack and short out. When that happens, the system may not switch off the front passenger airbag when it is supposed to.

item.title: Honda and Acura Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: In a wide range of Honda and Acura vehicles, the fuel pump located inside the fuel tank may fail. If it fails while you are driving, the engine can suddenly stall.

item.title: Acura, Honda Engine Bearing May Wear and Seize
item.description: These vehicles have an engine part called a connecting rod bearing, and a manufacturing error affects it. Because of this defect, the bearing can wear down over time and eventually seize up inside the engine. When that happens, the engine can become damaged. A damaged engine may not run the way it should, and it could even stop working suddenly while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Honda, Acura Models: Brake Master Cylinder May Separate
item.description: A fastener that connects the brake booster to the brake master cylinder may not have been put together correctly when the vehicle was built. Over time, this can cause the master cylinder to come apart from the booster assembly.

item.title: Acura Integra, RDX and Accord Brake Fluid Leak
item.description: On some Acura Integra, Acura RDX, and Honda Accord vehicles, a valve inside the brake system may leak brake fluid. This can cause the vehicle to move on its own when the brake hold feature is on, or make the brake pedal feel like it needs to be pushed further down than normal.

item.title: Honda, Acura Seat Belt Buckles May Not Latch
item.description: Certain Honda and Acura vehicles, including the CR-V, Accord, Accord Hybrid, Odyssey, Insight, and RDX, may have a manufacturing problem with the front seat belts. The buckle's channel may interfere with the release button, which can prevent the seat belt buckle from latching properly. This means the seat belt may not click into place and hold securely the way it is supposed to for the driver or front passenger seat.

item.title: Acura TLX Tires May Be Damaged
item.description: Honda says the tires on some Acura TLX vehicles may have been cut or torn during the sorting process. This tire damage can affect how the tires hold up on the road. Honda is recalling the affected vehicles so dealers can inspect the tires and replace them if necessary.

item.title: Acura RDX, Honda CR-V Hybrid Driveshaft May Fail
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Acura RDX and CR-V Hybrid vehicles because a part in the front driveshaft, on the right or left side, may not have been heat-treated correctly during manufacturing. If that part fails, it can cause a sudden loss of drive power to the wheels, or let the vehicle roll away on its own if parked without the parking brake applied. Either situation can increase the risk of a crash or injury.

item.title: Honda, Acura fuel pump may fail, stall engine
item.description: On many Honda and Acura models, the low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail. If it fails, the engine can stall while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Honda and Acura Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: Certain Honda and Acura vehicles have a low-pressure fuel pump, inside the fuel tank, that may fail. If the pump fails while you are driving, the engine can stall, which raises the risk of a crash. Honda will replace the fuel pump assembly on affected vehicles, free of charge, as part of this recall.

item.title: Acura ILX Driveshaft Can Separate From Half Shaft
item.description: Some Acura ILX vehicles have too much grease in a part called the half shaft. The excess grease can prevent a set-ring from fully engaging, which can allow the driveshaft to come apart from the half shaft.

item.title: Honda and Acura Models: Timing Belt May Fail
item.description: On certain Acura MDX, TLX, and Honda Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline vehicles, the teeth on the timing belt may separate from the belt. If the timing belt teeth separate, the engine may stall while driving. Honda will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the vehicle and replace the timing belt if it's affected. If a new timing belt is installed, the engine will also be inspected and any damaged parts will be replaced, all free of charge.

item.title: Acura MDX Taillights May Fail From Moisture
item.description: Some Acura MDX and MDX Sport Hybrid vehicles may let moisture into the tailgate lid lights. This can cause the tailgate lid lights and the taillights to stop working. Losing the taillights reduces how visible the vehicle is to others, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Acura MDX, TLX Fuel Pump May Cause Engine Stall
item.description: Certain Acura MDX and TLX vehicles have a problem with the fuel pump. Tiny particles in the fuel can stick to parts inside the pump over time, causing it to lose performance. When the fuel pump isn't working the way it should, it can make the engine stall while the vehicle is being driven. This kind of engine stall increases the risk of a crash, since it can happen while you are out on the road driving normally.

item.title: Acura ILX Fuel Gauge May Read Incorrectly
item.description: Some Acura ILX vehicles may have a fuel tank that is deformed, which raises the height of the fuel pump inside the tank. This can cause the fuel level float to stick, so the fuel gauge may show more fuel in the tank than there actually is. Because of this, the gauge reading may not match how much gas is really left in the tank.

item.title: Acura and Honda Models Have Reduced Brake Performance
item.description: On certain Acura MDX, Acura MDX Sport Hybrid, Honda HR-V, and Honda Odyssey vehicles, a coating inside the rear brake calipers may not have been applied correctly during manufacturing. This can allow small gas pockets to form inside the caliper pistons. Over time, these gas pockets can reduce how well the brakes are able to slow or stop the vehicle, lowering overall braking performance.

item.title: Honda and Acura Power Seats May Detach
item.description: On these vehicles, the powered front seats may have been built with rivets that were not manufactured correctly. This affects the driver and passenger seats in the Honda vehicles, and the driver seat in the Acura vehicles. In a crash, these rivets can break, which can cause the seat to come loose from the floor of the vehicle instead of staying secured in place.
